title: 478. Where was the Second Buddhist Council held?
hint: This ancient republic was important in Buddhist history.
summary: The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali.

title: 479. Which emperor patronized the Third Buddhist Council?
hint: He embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War.
summary: The Third Buddhist Council was held under Emperor Ashoka.

title: 480. The Third Buddhist Council was held at?

title: 481. Which Buddhist Council was held under Kanishka?
hint: It is associated with the rise of Mahayana Buddhism.
summary: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held under Kanishka.

title: 643. The concept of the 'Rule of Law' associated with Article 14 was given by:
hint: A British constitutional scholar.
summary: The concept of Rule of Law was propounded by A.V. Dicey.

title: 644. Which Fundamental Right has been described by the Supreme Court as the 'heart of fundamental rights' due to its broad interpretation?
hint: It protects life and personal liberty.
summary: Article 21 has received the widest judicial interpretation.

title: 645. Which landmark case established the 'Basic Structure Doctrine' of the Constitution?
hint: It was decided in 1973.
summary: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala established the Basic Structure Doctrine.

title: 1175. Which is the longest dam in India?
hint: It is located in Odisha.
summary: Hirakud Dam is the longest major dam in India.

title: 1176. Which dam is known as the 'Lifeline of Gujarat'?
hint: It is built across a west-flowing river.
summary: Sardar Sarovar Dam is popularly known as the Lifeline of Gujarat.

title: 1177. Which reservoir is formed by the Sardar Sarovar Dam?
hint: It has the same name as the dam.
summary: Sardar Sarovar Dam forms the Sardar Sarovar Reservoir.

title: 1178. Bhavanisagar Dam is constructed across which river?

title: What was Kondhana later called?

hint: It is located near Pune.
summary: Kondhana was renamed Sinhagad after Tanaji's death.

description: Which branch of Shivaji's military was developed to protect the western coastline?
hint: It consisted of ships and sailors.

title: 1491. Which Mauryan ruler fought the Kalinga War?
hint: His reign is known for numerous rock and pillar edicts.
summary: Ashoka fought the Kalinga War, traditionally dated to around 261 BCE, before adopting a stronger policy of Dhamma.

title: 1492. Which ancient kingdom was conquered by Ashoka in the famous Kalinga War?
hint: It was located largely in present-day Odisha.
summary: Kalinga, located largely in present-day Odisha and adjoining areas, was conquered by Ashoka after the Kalinga War.

title: 1493. What did Ashoka promote after the Kalinga War?
hint: It emphasized moral conduct and peaceful coexistence.
summary: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka strongly promoted Dhamma, emphasizing moral conduct, tolerance and welfare.

title: 1494. Which Buddhist council is traditionally associated with the reign of Ashoka?
hint: It was traditionally held at Pataliputra.
summary: According to Buddhist tradition, the Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra during Ashoka's reign.

title: 1383. Which of the following islands belongs to Lakshadweep?

summary: Kalpeni is one of the inhabited islands of Lakshadweep.

title: 1384. What is the official language used for administration in Lakshadweep?
hint: It is one of the official languages of India.
summary: Malayalam is widely used for administration in Lakshadweep, along with English.

title: 1385. Which of the following is a major environmental concern for Lakshadweep?
hint: It affects coral ecosystems.
summary: Coral bleaching due to climate change and rising sea temperatures is a major concern.

title: 24. The 'Din-i Ilahi' was a religious doctrine propounded by which Mughal emperor?
summary: Akbar introduced Din-i Ilahi to promote religious harmony among diverse faiths in the empire.

title: 25. Which act introduced the system of Dyarchy in Indian provinces?
summary: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced Dyarchy, dividing provincial subjects into Reserved and Transferred lists.

title: 26. The capital of the Cholas was located at which place?
summary: The Chola capital was at Thanjavur, later moved to Gangaikonda Cholapuram by Rajendra Chola.

title: Which architectural style is strongly associated with Chola temples?

hint: It developed prominently in the Tamil region.
summary: Chola temples are major examples of the Dravidian architectural tradition.

title: Which Chola temple is located at Gangaikondacholapuram?

hint: It is also known as the temple of Gangaikondacholisvaram.

title: Which Chola temple is located at Darasuram?
description: Identify the famous Chola temple situated at Darasuram near Kumbakonam.

summary: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was built during the reign of Rajaraja II.

title: 266. Which Wildlife Sanctuary in Assam is famous for golden langurs?

title: 267. Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary is famous for which animal?

title: 268. Which Wildlife Sanctuary in Odisha is famous for saltwater crocodiles?

title: 269. Which Wildlife Sanctuary in Maharashtra is famous for giant squirrels?
hint: Named after a Maratha ruler.
summary: Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary is known for the Indian giant squirrel.

title: 773. Which river crosses the Equator twice?

title: 774. Which is the longest river in Africa?

title: 776. Victoria Falls is located on which river?

title: 1311. Which was the first indigenously built aircraft carrier of India?
hint: It was commissioned in 2022.

title: 1312. Which missile is India's long-range surface-to-air missile developed jointly with Israel?
hint: It is also deployed by the Indian Navy.
summary: Barak-8 is jointly developed by India and Israel.

title: 1313. The headquarters of the Integrated Defence Staff (IDS) is located in:

title: 1314. Which Indian Air Force exercise is conducted jointly with the Royal Air Force (UK)?

title: 1315. Which missile is designed primarily as an anti-tank guided missile (ATGM)?
hint: It is named after a snake.

hint: It is in the northeastern Himalayan region.

title: 668. The Alps are primarily located in which continent?

title: 669. Which is the highest peak of the Alps?

summary: Mont Blanc is the highest peak in the Alps.

title: 670. Which mountain range separates Europe and Asia?

summary: The Ural Mountains traditionally form the boundary between Europe and Asia.

title: 1246. Which pass is located between Leh and the Indus Valley?

title: 1247. Which mountain pass is famous for the Sela Lake located nearby?
